result.type:

  n < p ^ a → k < p ^ a → ↑(n.choose k) ≡ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range a, ↑((n / p ^ i % p).choose (k / p ^ i % p)) [ZMOD ↑p]
result.value:
:= by
  apply (choose_modEq_choose_mul_prod_range_choose a).trans

result.informal_name: Lucas' Theorem for Binomial Coefficients Modulo a Prime
result.informal_description: For a prime $ p $ and integers $ n, k < p^a $, the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ is congruent modulo $ p $ to the product of binomial coefficients of the base-$ p $ digits of $ n $ and $ k $: $ \binom{n}{k} \equiv \prod_{i=0}^{a-1} \binom{n_i}{k_i} \mod p $, where $ n_i = \lfloor n/p^i \rfloor \mod p $ and $ k_i = \lfloor k/p^i \rfloor \mod p $.

result.informal_description: For a prime $ p $ and natural numbers $ n, k, a $, if $ n < p^a $ and $ k < p^a $, then the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ is congruent modulo $ p $ to the product of the binomial coefficients of the base-$ p $ digits of $ n $ and $ k $. Specifically, $ \binom{n}{k} \equiv \prod_{i=0}^{a-1} \binom{n_i}{k_i} \pmod{p} $, where $ n_i = \lfloor n/p^i \rfloor \mod p $ and $ k_i = \lfloor k/p^i \rfloor \mod p $ denote the base-$ p $ digits of $ n $ and $ k $.

name: Choose
choose_modEq_choose_mod_mul_choose_div_nat
result.signature: : choose n k ≡ choose (n % p) (k % p) * choose (n / p) (k / p) [MOD p]
result.type: ∀ {n k p : ℕ} [Fact (Nat.Prime p)], n.choose k ≡ (n % p).choose (k % p) * (n / p).choose (k / p) [MOD p]
result.informal_name: Lucas' Theorem for Binomial Coefficients Modulo a Prime
result.informal_description: For any prime number $ p $ and natural numbers $ n, k $, the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ satisfies the congruence $ \binom{n}{k} \equiv \binom{n \bmod p}{k \bmod p} \cdot \binom{\lfloor n/p \rfloor}{\lfloor k/p \rfloor} \pmod{p} $. This is the fundamental identity in Lucas' theorem, which decomposes binomial coefficients modulo primes using digit-wise operations in base $ p $.
